transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (CTO, Seraphic), Samir Khan (Cloud Architect), Priya Menon (Security Lead), Tom Wallace (PM)

[00:00] Maya: Hi everybody, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, with Liam our solutions engineer. Quick intro?
[00:12] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Hi, Elena here, CTO at Seraphic Health. Samir, Priya and Tom are on the call too.
[00:18] Samir: Samir Khan, cloud infra.
[00:20] Priya: Priya, security.
[00:22] Tom: Tom, product.
[00:25] Maya: Great. Goal for today is to scope the POC for private networking and data residency, get to success criteria, workload sizing, and a benchmark timeline.
[00:32] Liam: I'll add we'll sketch a bench plan — token rates, concurrency, and the regions we'll run in.
[00:40] Tom: Our top constraints are EU data residency, no customer data leaving EU, and minimal egress to third parties. Latency under 200ms for user-facing chat is a plus.
[00:50] Maya: Noted. Two primary networking options we surface: VPC peering (customer AWS <-> Redwood VPC) or AWS PrivateLink. Both are supported; peering is simpler for low-latency but requires route control, PrivateLink gives more control over endpoints.
[01:05] Priya: From security side, we prefer PrivateLink if it avoids internet egress. Also need KMS integration and audit logs retained for 12 months.
[01:14] Liam: We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; audit logs can be exported to your S3 or Splunk. There is an audit retention add-on if you need longer term.
[01:25] Dr. Elena Ruiz: For the POC, we want to validate throughput for our triage pipeline — about 40 simultaneous sessions, avg 350 tokens per session, burst to 120 concurrent. Also embed generation for search: ~10k embeddings/day batch.
[01:40] Samir: Our current infra is AWS eu-west-1, we want everything stay in EU. We can provide account IDs and VPC CIDRs.
[01:48] Maya: Perfect. For sizing, based on those numbers we'd suggest starting with 2x A100-class nodes in Dedicated private cluster or a private deployment on customer's VPC depending on latency needs.
[02:02] Liam: Rough math: 40 concurrent with 350 tokens average and 15 tps per GPU means you'll need headroom for bursts — plan for 2-3 GPUs for puyhey — sorry, planning for 3 GPUs to be safe. We'll put exact numbers in the bench spreadsheet.
[02:20] Tom: What's the expected per-token latency impact if we go quantized model vs fp16? We want cost down but can't hurt quality for triage decisions.
[02:30] Liam: Quantization to int8 typically lowers cost ~40-60% with a small latency improvement; quality can be impacted on some edge prompts. For the POC we can run both: fp16 baseline and int8 candidate, compare latency and sample outputs on your eval set.
[02:46] Priya: We need to be sure the models never hit public internet, even for auth calls. Is the control plane separated?
[02:52] Maya: With Private deployment we offer a customer-managed control plane; for Dedicated we have VPC options and control plane traffic can be routed via PrivateLink. We'll share the architecture doc.
[03:04] Samir: For VPC peering we need to know exact CIDR recommendations to avoid overlap. Also route table changes are needed; who owns NAT?
[03:12] Liam: Good question. If peered, you keep your NAT; egress rules are yours. PrivateLink keeps all traffic via endpoints, you don't need route changes but you do need to create interface endpoints in your subnets. We'll include step-by-step.
[03:26] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Benchmarks: we want to see p50/p95 latency for generation, throughput at sustained 10 RPS and burst to 40 RPS, plus mem use and tokenization differences. Also round-trip for embeddings batch of 10k.
[03:40] Liam: We'll design two bench scenarios: interactive chat (concurrency + latency) and batch embeddings. We'll capture p50/p90/p95, cost estimate /token, and failure modes.
[03:51] Maya: Acceptance criteria? What would make the POC a success for you?
[03:55] Tom: If latency p95 < 250ms for typical session and cost per 1k tokens within 20% of your predicted number, and no data egress outside EU, we consider it successful. Also ability to rotate KMS keys without downtime is important.
[04:10] Priya: Add: audit logs present and SAML SSO for users, RBAC enforced.
[04:16] Maya: Good. We'll capture these in the acceptance checklist.
[04:20] Samir: Timeline? We are aiming for a two-week POC starting next Monday. Is that feasible?
[04:26] Liam: If you can provide account IDs and CIDRs by Friday, we can provision infra and run bench in week one, analyze week two. That matches a two-week cycle.
[04:36] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Sounds good, but security team needs to review the security pack before infra touches prod accounts. We can use a sandbox account for the bench if needed.
[04:46] Priya: Yes, sandbox preferred. Also will want to run penetration-lite scans.
[04:50] Maya: We'll send the security pack with SOC2/ISO artifacts and architecture diagram. Sandbox is fine.
[04:56] Liam: Bench details: We'll need sample prompts and an eval set from you (sanitized). For embeddings, a representative dataset for latency calculation. We'll run both fp16 and int8 if you want quality comparisons.
[05:08] Tom: We'll sanitize and share a subset. How about eu-west-1 as the bench region?
[05:11] Maya: Agreed — EU region. We'll aim for bench window next Wednesday/Thursday, subject to you getting us network details.
[05:20] Samir: One question: egress to telemetry/metrics providers — we want to block any third-party telemetry. Can Redwood disable external telemetry?
[05:28] Liam: Yes, telemetry can be disabled in private deployments; in Dedicated we can route telemetry to your logging endpoints. We'll note that in the security pack.
[05:36] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Anything else around compliance? Data residency, encryption?
[05:40] Maya: We support customer-managed KMS, data at-rest encryption, and options to store logs in customer S3 in EU. We'll include details in the doc.
[05:50] Tom: What about failover / fallback if capacity constrained? We don't want calls to go to a hosted model outside EU.
[05:57] Liam: We'll set routing policies: prefer EU-only capacity; if a fallback is needed it's to another EU zone or to degrade gracefully (reject vs route). We'll include defaults and you can customize.
[06:08] Maya: Recap of next steps: Maya sends security pack + architecture, Liam shares bench plan & spreadsheet, Seraphic provides sandbox AWS account IDs + CIDR + sanitized eval data, then we schedule bench window.
[06:20] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Ok, we'll aim to have the account info and CIDRs by Friday.
[06:24] Priya: I'll review security docs and confirm egress rules.
[06:27] Samir: I'll prep network team for PrivateLink vs peering decisions.
[06:30] Maya: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench run and share the docs.
[06:36] Tom: Appreciate it, talk soon.
[06:38] Maya: Bye all.

Notes / Links referenced: private-deploy-checklist.pdf, redwood-sec-pack-2027.zip, bench-plan-template.xlsx (link), architecture-diagram-url

End of transcript.
